overview: Belize is a small country on the Caribbean coast of Central America, between Mexico and Guatemala. Its capital is Belmopan, but its largest city is Belize City. Belize was a British colony called British Honduras until it became independent in 1981, and it is the only country in Central America where English is the official language. It was an important part of the ancient Maya world.

geography.text: The north of Belize is low and flat, while the south rises into the Maya Mountains, and much of the country is covered by tropical forest. Just off the coast lies the Belize Barrier Reef, part of the second-largest reef system in the world, dotted with small islands called cayes and home to the famous Great Blue Hole.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Hot and humid, with a rainy season from June to November.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Jaguars, tapirs, howler monkeys and toucans, and the world's second-largest barrier reef.

history.text: Belize was part of the Maya world, with great cities such as Caracol and Lamanai. British loggers settled the coast in the 1600s, and it became the colony of British Honduras in 1862. It took the name Belize in 1973 and became independent in 1981, although neighbouring Guatemala long claimed its land.

events.title: British colony
events.text: The area becomes the colony of British Honduras.

events.title: Renamed Belize
events.text: The colony takes the name Belize.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Belize becomes independent despite Guatemala's claim.

government.text: Belize is a constitutional monarchy within the Commonwealth, with the British monarch as head of state, represented by a Governor-General. The Prime Minister leads the government. It is the only country in Central America where English is the official language. Guatemala has long claimed part of its territory, and the dispute is before the International Court of Justice.

economy.text: Tourism is Belize's biggest industry, drawn by its barrier reef, Maya ruins and rainforest. Sugar, bananas, citrus fruit and seafood are its main exports.

culture.text: Belize is a mix of peoples: Mestizo, Kriol, Maya, Garifuna, Mennonite and others. Garifuna language, dance and music are listed by UNESCO. The Belize Barrier Reef is the largest in the northern hemisphere and includes the Great Blue Hole, a vast underwater sinkhole.

items.title: Great Blue Hole
items.text: A round sinkhole in the sea about 300 m wide.

items.title: Caracol
items.text: A huge Maya city hidden in the jungle.

items.title: Garifuna culture
items.text: Music, dance and language listed by UNESCO.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Rice and beans with stewed chicken, and fry jacks, fried dough eaten at breakfast.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Punta rock, a modern version of Garifuna music, is Belize's own sound.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Garifuna Settlement Day, 19 November, re-enacts the Garifuna arrival by boat in 1832.

sport.text: Football and basketball are the most popular sports in Belize. Its biggest sporting event is the Cross Country Cycling Classic, held every Easter since 1928.

items.title: Cross Country Classic
items.text: A one-day cycle race held every Easter Saturday.

items.title: La Ruta Maya
items.text: A four-day canoe race across the country.

didYouKnow: Belize was the first country in the world to create a jaguar reserve, in 1984.
Belize is the only country in Central America with English as its official language.

keyPeople.name: Andy Palacio
keyPeople.text: Brought Garifuna music to the world.
